title: Papermaking: The Historical Diffusion of an Ancient Technique
locator: Mobilities of Knowledge, chapter 3, pp. 51–66; inspected pp. 51–64, especially 52–54 and 63–64; full text also inspected in ResearchGate PDF mirror.
scope_limit: Comparative survey with some conjectural transmission and preference explanations. The underlying medieval documents were not independently inspected. No precise first, Talas explanation, India/West Africa preference claim, or universal hydraulic-mill lineage is adopted.
evidence_lineage: Synthesises the author's Paper Before Print (2001), not directly read here, and earlier scholarship. Tunis watermark evidence is inherited from Valls i Subirà (1970); the Ibn Marzuq ruling from Halevi (2008) and Lagardère (1995). The European paper-property discussion draws on Barrett, also NET-S02, so these are not independent corroborations.

title: European Papermaking Techniques 1300–1800
locator: University of Iowa, Paper Through Time; dated August 2011; inspected Introduction, Raw Materials/Water, and Sizing.
scope_limit: Author explicitly calls parts of this a generalisation and hypothesis from limited early records, later craft descriptions and practical experience; not a census of historical mills or a measured adoption series.
evidence_lineage: Reworks Barrett's 1989 essay and combines historical-paper research, personal papermaking experience, and eighteenth-century descriptions by Lalande, Goussier and Desmarest. Shared material foundation with Bloom NET-S01; not a separate medieval documentary sample.

title: Material properties of Islamic paper
locator: Heritage Science 4:34, DOI 10.1186/s40494-016-0103-4; inspected pp. 1–3, 9–10 and collection/method limitations.
scope_limit: 228-paper conservation reference collection; 133 undated; most dated samples much later than medieval diffusion. Abstract and methods describe chronology differently. Unknown provenance/storage limits inference; used to bound attribution, not measure medieval uptake.
evidence_lineage: Original laboratory analyses of a UCL reference collection; the same physical papers underpin all reported analytical methods. Independent material research but not an independent medieval chronology. Historical background draws on earlier codicological literature.

title: A Selection of Shen Gua's Writings in Translation, appendix 3 to Shen Gua's Empiricism
locator: Appendix pp. 22–24, section on movable-type printing, with notes 67–71; original Brush Talks from Dream Brook, late eleventh century, describing 1041–1048.
scope_limit: Historical testimony in a modern scholarly translation. Described efficiency is Shen's assessment, not a modern replication result. The main 2018 book was not inspected. Translator's clay-composition debate is not adjudicated here.
evidence_lineage: Translation of Shen's Mengxi bitan passage with Chinese text and modern annotation. This is the same frequently cited historical account underlying many claims about Bi Sheng; repetition by later historians is not independent eyewitness corroboration.

title: Introduction, The Book Worlds of East Asia and Europe, 1450–1850: Connections and Comparisons
locator: Publisher preview includes introduction pp. 1–64; inspected pp. 11–15 and 17–24, with references and relevant figures' captions.
scope_limit: Selected chapter pages, not entire edited book. Comparative cost statements are qualitative and heterogeneous across periods. Some early European type-casting details and transfer claims are disputed. No uniform cross-civilisation cost ratio is inferred.
evidence_lineage: Technology/workflow comparison synthesises McDermott (2006), Chia, Brokaw, Chow, Tsien, Gaskell and others. Ricci's cost remark is inherited testimony, not an independent price series. Chinese movable-type origin ultimately overlaps NET-S04. Much European production history also overlaps sources inherited by NET-S09/S10.

title: Buddhist texts: The Diamond Sutra
locator: Sections The Diamond Sutra, How and why was it made?, and Colophon from the Diamond Sutra; object Or.8210/P.2, dated 11 May 868.
scope_limit: Custodian's object description and translated colophon inspected; no independent material examination or original-Chinese collation. Earliest-dated-survivor language does not identify invention or actual distribution volume.
evidence_lineage: The physical scroll and its colophon are the underlying record. This institutional page and other Diamond Sutra webpages describe the same object and are not independent witnesses to diffusion.

title: Jikji, a treasure of the world of printing
locator: Sections What is Jikji?, A treasure of humanity, From Korea to France, and Preservation and access; BnF Coréen 109.
scope_limit: Custodian description of a surviving second volume and a 1378 xylograph counterpart. Does not establish print-run size, commercial success, widespread literacy or the earliest-ever use of metal type.
evidence_lineage: Underlying surviving 1377 Jikji volume/colophon and Korean 1378 woodblock edition. UNESCO recognition is not an independent experiment; Park's mention of Jikji in NET-S08 refers to the same artifact tradition.

title: Manuscript, Not Print, in the Book World of Chosŏn Korea (1392–1910)
locator: The Routledge Companion to Korean Literature, chapter 1, pp. 19–38; inspected pp. 19–28 and conclusion pp. 34–35, especially pp. 22–27 and p. 27 n. 16.
scope_limit: Selected full chapter within a publisher preview, not entire volume. Combines historiographical critique and case-based manuscript research; no representative readership, literacy or wage series. Later examples are identified as subepisodes, not evidence for fourteenth-century diffusion.
evidence_lineage: Re-examines Courant's Korean Bibliography and scholarship on surviving vernacular and literary manuscripts. Rental chronology relies on earlier studies and literati accounts; state/private examples cite Walraven (2007) and No (2013), not directly read here. Comparative framing partly draws on NET-S05 and shared book-history literature.

title: Information Technology and Economic Change: The Impact of the Printing Press
locator: Quarterly Journal of Economics 126:1133–1172, DOI 10.1093/qje/qjr035; inspected pp. 1133–44, 1153–56 and §V.E (pp. 1157 onward), especially Table I and nn. 20–23, 38, 40.
scope_limit: City-level historical data and conditional instrumental-variable design, not national productivity or welfare. Table I's historical-city denominator differs from regression samples. Some production-history details are inherited and contested; mature casting should not be projected intact into 1450.
evidence_lineage: Adoption compilation combines ISTC (1998), Febvre and Martin (1958), Clair (1976); populations from Bairoch, Batou and Chèvre (1988). The 205-city list and 27,873 edition records are not separate independent uptake samples. Shared historical foundations and arguments recur in NET-S10.

title: New Media and Competition: Printing and Europe's Transformation after Gutenberg
locator: CEP Discussion Paper 1600, January 2019; inspected pp. 1–7, §3.1 and price/competition and identification discussions in §§5–7; p. 3 summarises price results.
scope_limit: Working-paper version, not assumed identical to later publication. Introduction reports over 295,000 publications; §3.1 over 299,000 editions. Edition counts are not copies, sales or readers; prices have a separate selected purchasing-record sample. Exclusion restrictions require scrutiny.
evidence_lineage: USTC 2012 editions; Hoock/Jeannin merchants' manuals; Hernando Colón purchase records; printer biographies including Reske; publications naming heirs/widows. Distinct evidence layers but not independent replications of one causal result. Reuses NET-S09's adoption history/cost account; printer-death measures have different survival selection.

title: Did Ottoman Sultans Ban Print?
locator: Book History 20:1–39, DOI 10.1353/bh.2017.0000; inspected pp. 1–11, 16–20, 22–29 and associated notes; documentary core pp. 6–11.
scope_limit: No surviving general ban is not proof of no restriction. Interpretation is scoped to the alleged Bayezid/Selim bans and extant 1588/1727 documents. Original Ottoman documents not independently read; translations and close reading are Schwartz's.
evidence_lineage: Traces inherited ban claims through Thevet, Guignes, Cheikho and Lewis, so their repeated assertion is one transmission chain. Documentary counterevidence is the 1588 firman reproduced in a 1594 Euclid and Müteferrika's 1729 prefatory firman/fatwa materials. Uses Sabev critically; not an independent archive of his probate quantities.

title: Formation of Ottoman Print Culture (1726–1746): Some General Remarks
locator: New Europe College Regional Program 2003–2004, 2004–2005, pp. 293–333; inspected pp. 293, 299–307 and relevant notes.
scope_limit: Uses sixteen-edition grouping; appendices/titles need not equal other catalogues' counts. Three print runs estimated. Stock depletion is not observed sales; gifts and unequal time on market matter. Probate reader sample restricted to Istanbul askeri decedents with more than three books, not population literacy.
evidence_lineage: Original research on Müteferrika's probate inventory and selected Istanbul Askeriye probate registers, plus initial-run statements and contemporary observers. Later percentage claims often recycle this one estate reconstruction. This contribution did not inspect the original register or count its entries independently.

title: Indian Ocean navigation in Islamic sources 850–1560 CE
locator: History Compass 16:e12485, DOI 10.1111/hic3.12485; author-uploaded full-text extraction inspected, especially §§2–4, pp. 2–7.
scope_limit: Primarily Arabic/Turkish textual corpus, not representative of all Indian Ocean crews. Chronology of surviving detailed texts is not invention chronology. No instrument-carriage or accident denominator. Do not use incidental ancient-compass or first-crossing claims.
evidence_lineage: Synthesis of Ibn Majid, al-Mahri and Sidi Ali Reis through editions/translations, especially Tibbetts and Khoury, plus Portuguese testimony. Shares core manuscript corpus with NET-S14 and partly the voyage tradition of NET-S15. Translation bias and neglect of Arabic editions are explicitly discussed.

title: Reflections on the Knowledge of Shallow Waters
locator: Isis 112(1), DOI 10.1086/713561; full HTML essay inspected; especially paragraphs beginning It appears that early Portuguese sailors, Curiously, and Where the Chinese compass.
scope_limit: Comparative reflection, not a measured compass-carriage survey. Its generalisation that the Islamic world resisted print is excluded in light of NET-S11. Potential naming/conflation issues in its compressed navigation genealogy are not used.
evidence_lineage: Uses Ibn Majid via Tibbetts and the author's prior maritime research, overlapping NET-S13's core texts. Chinese comparisons depend on Papelitzky's separate essay, not inspected here. Agreement on navigational practices is therefore not two independent fleet samples.

title: A Journal of the First Voyage of Vasco da Gama, 1497–1499
locator: Hakluyt Society translation, public-domain electronic transcription; inspected voyage narrative pp. 40–47, especially 45–47 (Malindi, 22–24 April 1498 and Arabian Sea crossing).
scope_limit: Translation of a surviving manuscript tradition, not an unmediated modern log. Anonymous attribution and editorial brackets are retained as such. Christian identifications are unreliable for religion/ethnicity; no identification of the pilot with Ibn Majid is made. One episode cannot measure fleet-level dependence.
evidence_lineage: Anonymous Roteiro narrative mediated by Ravenstein's nineteenth-century edition. Staples discusses the same voyage tradition, so this checks the narrated episode directly in translation but is not an independent second voyage. Editorial notes are distinguished from the historical narrator.
